correction_patch: P1.1 SCENARIO CONTRACT CORRECTION (small patch; no P1 redesign)

p1_1_corrections.subject: F3 rule classification
p1_1_corrections.was: Every supplied non-empty victory_rule_id / defeat_rule_id was emitted as CALLER_DECLARED_LOCAL.
p1_1_corrections.why_wrong: A bare supplied string carries no information about whether it denotes a real game rule, an unknown identifier or a caller-owned local rule, and the pre-P1 contract defines no caller-owned rule input. Classifying it as caller-owned was not justified.
p1_1_corrections.now: absent/null/empty -> UNSPECIFIED; non-empty string -> UNKNOWN; non-string -> ScenarioCompileError. resolved_rule/authority stay null and execution_semantics stays NONE. CALLER_DECLARED_LOCAL remains in the vocabulary but is unreachable from the current bare-string input.

p1_1_corrections.subject: Scenario package schema version
p1_1_corrections.was: Emitted hsr_battle_agent.scenario_package/1 while replacing the bare rules.victory_rule_id / defeat_rule_id strings with structured records.
p1_1_corrections.why_wrong: Replacing a field shape is not purely additive, so retaining /1 silently re-interpreted the contract.
p1_1_corrections.now: Emits hsr_battle_agent.scenario_package/2. The ambiguous bare-string fields are NOT restored. LEGACY_PACKAGE_SCHEMA records the superseded /1 shape.

documented.scenario_package/1: pre-P1 static shape (rules echoed bare victory_rule_id / defeat_rule_id strings)
documented.scenario_package/2: P0 static monster-resolution metadata + P1 explicit rule records + wave identity/origin/provenance contract

p1_1_corrections.subject: Audit defect numbering
p1_1_corrections.was: P1-owned text stated that F5 was closed by the wave-overlay work.
p1_1_corrections.why_wrong: Audit F5 is LOADOUT COMPLETENESS and remains untouched. P1 closes F2, F3 and F4 only; wave-id retention and override provenance are part of F4 closure.
p1_1_corrections.now: Corrected in the scenario_compiler.py docstring, HANDOFF_MANIFEST.json, this control artifact, the contract document and the test module docstrings. No F5 implementation was added or modified.
p1_1_corrections.f5_verification: A dedicated test class asserts that no six-relic-slot rule is enforced and that skill_levels / trace rank_state / initial_state are still carried without validation, i.e. F5 behaviour is unchanged.

p1_1_corrections.subject: Contract acceptance wording
p1_1_corrections.was: free_scenario_assembly_contract_v1.json claimed template compatibility includes addING/REMOVING enemies or Buffs.
p1_1_corrections.why_wrong: P1 implements no enemy or Buff removal mechanism, so the acceptance statement overstated the contract.
p1_1_corrections.now: The statement matches reality: template waves are retained by default; a matching caller wave_index replaces that wave's enemy set; a new caller wave_index adds a wave; template wave_id/provenance is retained; caller Buff bindings may be added and template Buff bindings remain. Removal is explicitly NOT claimed.

p1_1_corrections.subject: Golden / execution safety
p1_1_corrections.reviewed: golden_eligible is a static formula: not unresolved_behavior and unsupported_policy != 'opaque-disabled'. It never consults rule resolution.
p1_1_corrections.confirmed: An UNKNOWN rule cannot be read as resolved or executable: resolution_status is never RESOLVED, resolved_rule and authority stay null, and execution_semantics is always NONE.
p1_1_corrections.deferred_requirement: Once behavior gaps can close (a later behavior-execution CR), golden/executable eligibility MUST additionally require every rule reference to be RESOLVED. Today every compiled package has at least one unresolved behavior gap (an AvatarBehavior/MonsterBehavior/StageBuffBehavior entry per entity), so golden_eligible is always false and the missing gate is currently unreachable rather than satisfied.
p1_1_corrections.scope: Recorded as a deferred gate requirement only; no behavior execution was added.

final_contract_sync.scope: P1.1 FINAL CONTRACT SYNC ONLY -- documentation wording; no Python, frontend, M10-M15, semantics or test change

contradictions_fixed.subject: input wording for victory_rule_id / defeat_rule_id
contradictions_fixed.was: the input description called a supplied id an 'optional caller-declared victory/defeat rule identifier'
contradictions_fixed.why_wrong: a bare string carries no authority or ownership information, so it must not be described as caller-declared
contradictions_fixed.now: described as an optional victory/defeat rule reference; a bare string carries no authority or ownership information and is recorded as UNKNOWN (absent/null/empty -> UNSPECIFIED)

contradictions_fixed.subject: dsh_implementation_contract immutability sentence
contradictions_fixed.was: stated that the ScenarioCompiler 'produces an immutable ScenarioPackage'
contradictions_fixed.why_wrong: P1 explicitly decided IMMUTABILITY_DEFERRED, so the contract claimed a guarantee the code does not make
contradictions_fixed.now: states the actual guarantee -- deterministic, self-contained, copy-isolated, stable package_sha256 -- and states that immutable product typing is deferred hardening

player_team_bound.party_order_semantics_added: NONE -- supplied slot identity is preserved verbatim; no gameplay party-order semantics were introduced

rule_resolution_representation.decision: Every victory/defeat rule reference is emitted as an explicit resolution record; bare rule-id strings are no longer echoed anywhere in the package.
rule_resolution_representation.chosen_outcome: B -- UNKNOWN for a supplied identifier; UNSPECIFIED when absent. Option C (CALLER_DECLARED_LOCAL) is deliberately NOT reachable because no typed local-rule input exists in the contract.
rule_resolution_representation.rationale: The static content layer has no victory/defeat rule catalogue (checked: the SQLite facade exposes no rule table; mode_metadata holds mode/challenge metadata only; the only rule-like tokens are opaque stage-authored level_win_condition/level_lose_condition strings). No supplied identifier can be promoted to RESOLVED, and a bare string cannot be shown to be caller-owned, so the honest classification is UNKNOWN.
rule_resolution_representation.no_invented_semantics: No rule was mapped to any semantics; resolved_rule and authority stay null and execution_semantics stays NONE.
rule_resolution_representation.no_terminal_policy_mapping: A scenario rule reference is never mapped onto an M10 terminal policy automatically.

rule_execution_gate.requirement: golden/executable eligibility must additionally require every rule reference to be RESOLVED
rule_execution_gate.current_behaviour: golden_eligible = (not unresolved_behavior) and (unsupported_policy != 'opaque-disabled'); rule resolution is not consulted
rule_execution_gate.why: Every compiled package carries at least one BEHAVIOR_COMPILATION_REQUIRED gap (one per Avatar, Monster and StageBuff), so unresolved_behavior is never empty and golden_eligible is always false today
rule_execution_gate.owner: a future behavior-execution CR; explicitly out of scope for P1/P1.1

template_overlay_semantics.decision: The resolved Stage template establishes the base ordered wave set; caller waves are overlaid, never replacing the template.
rule: template waves establish the base ordered wave set
a caller wave whose wave_index matches a template wave REPLACES that wave's enemies and keeps the template wave identity
a caller wave with a previously unseen wave_index is ADDED
template waves the caller does not mention are RETAINED
template_overlay_semantics.removal_mechanism: None exists in this contract and none was invented; an omitted template wave is always retained.
template_overlay_semantics.ordering: compiled waves are sorted by wave_index (deterministic)

wave_id_retention.decision: Every compiled wave carries wave_index AND wave_id, plus origin and override_applied.

wave_id_values.overridden_template_wave: the Stage template wave_id (template identity retained)

wave_id_retention.fabricated_native_wave_id: NEVER -- a caller-created wave never receives a manufactured game wave_id

provenance_semantics.decision: A minimal explicit per-wave provenance block; no second general provenance framework was introduced.
provenance_semantics.enemy_level: Each enemy keeps its existing template_position {group_index, slot} and carries origin mirroring the wave origin; full source envelopes are not duplicated.
provenance_semantics.reuse: Existing Source Package source_refs / entity envelopes are reused; the top-level source_stage block is unchanged.

scenario_schema_decision.subject: the rules block shape changed from bare victory_rule_id / defeat_rule_id strings to structured victory_rule / defeat_rule records
scenario_schema_decision.rationale: Replacing the bare rule strings with structured records is not purely additive, so the version was bumped rather than silently re-interpreted. No exact-shape production consumer exists in the repository (checked across .py/.ts/.tsx/.js/.json/.md: only this control artifact, the audit handoff and scenario_compiler.py reference the scenario package), so this is the low-cost migration window.
scenario_schema_decision.v2_definition: P0 static monster-resolution metadata + P1 explicit rule records + wave identity/origin/provenance contract

immutability_decision.rationale: A frozen product type would change the type identity of every returned package and would have to survive deepcopy/pickle and json-based stable_hash; that is a broad consumer risk rather than a local change, and the CR permits deferral.
immutability_decision.provided_instead: deterministic package_sha256 + copy isolation (the returned package is deep-copied so it shares no mutable container with the caller request or the database facade)
immutability_decision.f6_status: recorded only; not expanded into a redesign

changed_files.change: F2 player-team bound; F3 explicit rule-resolution records with non-empty string -> UNKNOWN; F4 deterministic Stage-template wave overlay with wave_id and provenance retention; PACKAGE_SCHEMA bumped to scenario_package/2 with LEGACY_PACKAGE_SCHEMA; docstring numbering corrected (F2/F3/F4 only, F5 explicitly untouched); copy-isolated return.

50 focused tests: team bound, rule resolution (UNKNOWN mapping, UNSPECIFIED, CALLER_DECLARED_LOCAL unreachable, execution_semantics NONE), template overlay, wave-id retention, F5-untouched proofs, rule-execution safety, P0 regression, determinism, static boundary, schema /2 decision, real-database conformance.

The pre-P1 test test_stage_template_can_be_overridden_without_flattening_waves asserted the audited (replace) behaviour, waves == [7]; it is renamed and updated to the contract-conformant overlay expectation [1, 7] with wave_id/origin/override_applied assertions. Unchanged by the P1.1 patch.

Static contract documentation synchronised with the implemented compiler: optional caller wave_id on enemy_waves; rule ids described as references that a bare string leaves UNKNOWN; added compiler requirements; a static_contract_conformance block recording the team bound, the UNKNOWN rule mapping with its input table, the deferred rule-execution gate, the template overlay, wave identity retention and the scenario_package/2 schema decision; template_compatibility reworded to drop the enemy/Buff removal claim. Final P1.1 sync removed the residual 'caller-declared' input wording and replaced the 'immutable ScenarioPackage' sentence with the actual deterministic/self-contained/copy-isolated/stable-hash guarantee plus the IMMUTABILITY_DEFERRED note. No dynamic/behavior claim was altered.
